MMDR AMENDMENT BILL 2026: CENTRE CLARIFIES STATES’ MINING REVENUE & RIGHTS REMAIN PROTECTED

📌 Bill aims to regulate taxation on mineral-bearing land, not land rights.

💰 States will continue to receive ~90% of mining-sector revenue — no reduction after the amendment.

✅ Existing revenue streams including royalty, auction premium, DMF benefits and GST share remain intact.

⚖️ Move seeks to address very high additional taxes imposed by some states, on top of 14 existing taxes, charges, fees & levies.

🏗️ Regulation of nearly 50 minor minerals remains completely with State Governments and is unaffected by the Bill.

🟢 Impact: Positive for Mining Sector — greater taxation clarity while protecting states’ existing revenue and regulatory powers.

AI Data Centre Value chain | India Picks & Shovels Map

1. Compute Engine
- Netweb Technologies: AI GPU servers.
- E2E Networks: GPU cloud infrastructure.
- Orient Technologies: GPU and cloud infrastructure.
- Panache Digilife: AI servers and hardware.
- Netweb AI systems: ~62% of Q1FY27 revenue.

2. Electrical Infrastructure
- Marine Electricals: MV/LV panels.
- Vivid Electromech: PDU and panels.
- RMC Switchgears: DC control panels.
- Schneider Electric Infrastructure: switchgear and distribution.
- Marine receives repeat data-centre orders.
- Vivid: ~50% FY26 revenue from data centres.

3. Cables & Fibre
- APAR Industries: LV/MV DC cables.
- Polycab: power, control and fibre cables.
- KEI Industries: LV/MV/EHV cables.
- RR Kabel: power and fire-safe cables.
- HFCL: AI data-centre connectivity.
- Sterlite Technologies: high-density fibre.
- APAR approved for major US DC projects.
- HFCL investing ₹215 Cr in connectivity.

4. Grid & Transformers
- Hitachi Energy India: transformers and GIS.
- GE Vernova T&D: transformers and grid equipment.
- Shilchar Technologies: customised transformers.
- CG Power: transformers and switchgear.
- Voltamp Transformers: transformers.
- AI expansion requires substantial grid infrastructure.
- More AI means higher power demand.
- Higher power demand drives transformer demand.

5. Cooling & Thermal Management
- KRN Heat Exchanger: cooling systems.
- Aeroflex Industries: liquid-cooling systems.
- Thermax: cooling and thermal infrastructure.
- Blue Star: chillers and precision cooling.
- Amber Enterprises: HVAC ecosystem.
- United Heat Exchanger: DC cooling.
- Aeroflex started AI/DC liquid-cooling dispatches.
- Thermax disclosed ₹400+ Cr US DC order.
- Higher GPU density increases cooling demand.

6. Water Infrastructure
- Ion Exchange: water treatment and reuse.
- Thermax: water and cooling infrastructure.
- VA Tech Wabag: high-purity water systems.
- Effwa Infra: emerging DC water opportunity.
- Cooling increases water-management requirements.
- Water recycling can reduce resource intensity.
- Thermal management remains closely linked.

7. Backup Power
- Powerica: large DG systems.
- Prostarm Info Systems: UPS and batteries.
- Cummins India: standby generation.
- Kirloskar Oil Engines: DG systems.
- Amara Raja: industrial and UPS batteries.
- Exide Industries: backup batteries.
- Hyperscale data centres require high reliability.
- UPS and batteries protect against outages.
- DG systems provide extended backup.

AI Data Centre Value Chain
- AI GPUs drive compute demand.
- Compute requires reliable electricity.
- Electricity requires transformers and switchgear.
- Power distribution requires cables and PDUs.
- GPUs generate substantial heat.
- Cooling systems manage thermal loads.
- Cooling requires water infrastructure.
- Backup systems protect against outages.

Key Themes
- AI expansion drives data-centre capacity.
- Data-centre capacity drives power demand.
- Power demand drives grid investment.
- GPU density drives cooling demand.
- Reliability drives backup-power investment.
- Water efficiency becomes increasingly important.

Key Monitorables
- Data-centre capacity additions.
- AI GPU deployments.
- Transformer order books.
- Cable demand growth.
- Cooling-system orders.
- Liquid-cooling adoption.
- UPS and battery demand.
- Data-centre power requirements.
- Water-treatment opportunities.

Key Takeaway
- The AI data-centre opportunity extends far beyond GPUs and semiconductors. India's AI infrastructure build-out can create a broad picks-and-shovels opportunity across transformers, switchgear, cables, fibre, cooling, water treatment, UPS, batteries and backup power. As AI workloads increase power density, the companies supplying the physical infrastructure required to build and operate data centres could become important beneficiaries of the AI capex cycle.

IFB INDUSTRIES Q1 CONCALL: TARGETS 20% FY27 REVENUE GROWTH; ₹110 CR CAPEX PLANNED 🏭📈

• 🎯 Management working towards ~20% revenue growth in FY27, supported by strong Home Appliances momentum

• 🏠 Home Appliances revenue grew 18% in Q1, with July also starting strongly

• ⚠️ Margins remain under pressure from commodity costs & forex headwinds

• 💰 Higher revenue, operating leverage and ongoing cost-saving initiatives expected to support margin recovery

• 🏭 FY27 capex planned at around ₹110 Cr

• ⚙️ Engineering division has a larger ~₹400 Cr stamping capacity expansion plan, to be deployed as new business is secured

• 🚀 New Home Appliance products expected over the next 3–6 months, alongside stronger distribution and in-store presence

ASHOK LEYLAND Q1 CONCALL: CV DEMAND OUTLOOK STRONG; Q2 MARGINS FACE COMMODITY PRESSURE 🚛📈

• 🚚 Management expects MHCV industry to grow high single digits in FY27, with LCV growth expected to be slightly better

• 📈 Q2 demand expected to be stronger than Q1, with positive momentum seen in July & August

• ⚠️ Q2 margins could remain under pressure due to peak commodity prices

• 💰 Price hikes, cost savings and better product mix being used to offset commodity inflation

• 📉 Commodity prices expected to soften from Q3 FY27, providing margin relief

• 👥 Manpower costs expected to rise 4–5% from Q2, while management targets tighter control over other overheads

• ⚙️ Upcoming regulations including mandatory AC and advanced braking could increase vehicle costs, but management expects positive TCO benefits for customers

• 🏭 Building capacity to manufacture 850 passenger coaches annually by FY29-30

• 🚇 Passenger rail outlook remains strong, supported by plans to expand metro coverage from 25 to 50 cities

• 📈 Government's target to increase freight loading to 3 billion tonnes expected to drive long-term wagon demand

• 🏭 Pursuing backward integration into solar cells, ingots & wafers

• ⚡ Plans to expand into ancillary products including transformers & inverters, evolving into an integrated energy platform

• 📊 Strategy aims to increase Saatvik’s value contribution in a solar project from ~25% currently to 40–50%

TD Power Systems Limited ("TDPS") has entered
into a Build-to-Print Manufacturing Framework Agreement dated August 13, 2026 with Siemens
Energy, Inc. ("Siemens Energy"), pursuant to which TDPS will manufacture and supply 2-pole
Generators in accordance with Siemens Energy's designs, drawings and specifications.

In simple words

TD Power has signed a 10 year deal with Siemens Energy's US arm to build large 2-pole generators for Siemens.

Siemens gives the designs and drawings, TDPS manufactures them. Siemens is doing this because its own factories are full (the AI data-centre power boom has its order books stuffed for years), so it needs someone qualified to make machines on its behalf. 

TDPS has licensed Siemens' 2-pole technology for over a decade, so this is that relationship getting upgraded from "we borrow your design" to "we are your factory."

Business only comes through individual purchase orders whenever Siemens issues them. So nothing goes into the order book today, and since these machines take 18–20 months to build, real revenue starts showing up around FY29. 

Also, since TDPS is building to Siemens' design and not its own, it doesn't own the technology and likely earns a thinner margin per unit  but with far higher volume, less design risk and better factory utilisation. 

Think of it as TDPS becoming a "CDMO for generators" for one of the world's top three turbine makers: strategically a very strong position, but for now it's a licence to receive orders, not the orders themselves.

Reliance Industries and Rolls-Royce announce strategic intent to partner and develop India's indigenous combat engine for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme

London / Mumbai, 14thAugust 2026: Reliance Industries Limited (Reliance) and Rolls-Royce (LSE: RR., ADR: RYCEY) today announced their strategic intent to partner and offer capabilities for the design, development, manufacturing and delivery of a sovereign indigenous combat engine for India’s Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme.

As part of the partnership, Reliance and Rolls-Royce will explore the formation of a dedicated Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex that will be a centre of excellence for power and propulsion technology in India.

The partnership will offer a compelling proposition for joint development of the AMCA engine in India, bringing together world-leading technology and industrial execution capabilities. This marks a step towards realising the vision set out by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, for India’s defence ecosystem to deliver an indigenous engine to power the country’s fighter jet programme.

Magellanic Cloud Limited’s Wholly Owned Subsidiary Provigil Surveillance Limited Receives ₹3.73 Cr LOA from PSU Major DFCCIL

• Order Value: ₹3.73 Cr from Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL).

• Scope: Supply, Installation, Testing & Commissioning (SITC) and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) of an E-Surveillance System across a section of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC).

• Tenure: 5-year contract on an OPEX model.

• Key Scope: E-surveillance for theft prevention, remote monitoring, asset & facility protection, perimeter security, dock management and Command & Control Centre services.

• Project Location: Kishangarh Balawas – New Rewari – New Phulera – New Kishangarh – Madar section of WDFC.

KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Limited Delivers Triple-Digit Growth in Q1 FY27

📌Q1 FY27 Consolidated Key Financial Highlights
- Revenue from Operations of ₹252.32 Cr, YoY growth of 118.87%
- EBITDA of ₹49.06 Cr, YoY growth of 178.85%
- EBITDA Margin of 19.44%, up 418 bps YoY
- Net Profit of ₹32.90 Cr, YoY growth of 164.84%
- Net Profit Margin of 13.04%, up 266 bps YoY

📌Q1 FY27 Standalone Key Financial Highlights
- Revenue from Operations of ₹181.97 Cr, YoY growth of 59.07%
- EBITDA of ₹24.67 Cr, YoY growth of 24.67%
- Net Profit of ₹18.67 Cr, YoY growth of 19.02%

📌Key Business Highlights
- Overseas revenue grew 177.31% YoY to ₹52.38 Cr, with exports contributing 20.76% of segment revenue
- Domestic revenue stood at ₹199.94 Cr, up 107.42% YoY
- Exports were spread across 14 countries, with the USA, France, Vietnam, UAE and Italy among the key markets
- ₹350 Cr QIP completed during the quarter, with net proceeds of ₹341.79 Cr. The funds raised have been allocated towards the stated objective

RECODE STUDIOS OPENS FIRST MODERN TRADE STORE; PLANS 15–20 MORE IN FY27 🚀

• 🏬 Opened its first NewU store at The Opulent Mall, Ghaziabad.

• 🤝 Partnership with NewU, the beauty & personal care retail chain operated by H&B Stores, a Dabur India subsidiary.

• 📈 Targets 15–20 additional NewU stores over the next 12 months across high-potential markets.

reports.text:
JPMORGAN ON GODREJ CONSUMER

• Rating: Overweight | Target: ₹1,175

• Surprise CEO resignation creates near-term uncertainty; CFO takes over as CEO

• Leadership transition likely to weigh on the share price in the short term

• Valuation multiples could compress until confidence in new leadership improves

• Internal succession reduces the risk of execution disruption

CITI ON GODREJ CONSUMER

• Rating: Accumulate | Target: ₹1,350

• Sudden CEO exit likely to weigh on near-term sentiment

• “Candor” and “pace” comments point to focus on transparency, accountability and faster execution

• Promoter expectations may have been higher in certain areas

• Leadership change creates a near-term overhang, but no evidence of a strategic reset

• Focus remains on improving execution within the existing strategy

MACQUARIE ON ZYDUS LIFE

• Rating: Outperform | Target: ₹1,285

• Q1 delivered an operational beat

• Management maintains FY27 guidance

• Consumer business expected to deliver double-digit growth in FY27

MACQUARIE ON HOSPITAL SECTOR 🏥

• Sees greater pricing oversight along with support for capex-intensive healthcare infrastructure

• Parliamentary committee recommendations are more interventionist than earlier policy discussions

• Report flags private healthcare as a major contributor to out-of-pocket spending and affordability concerns

• Reiterates UNDERPERFORM on Apollo Hospitals and Max Healthcare

JPMORGAN ON SIEMENS

• Rating: Underweight | Target: ₹3,334

• Margin pressure partly offset by healthy order inflows

• Q1FY27 demand remained strong with robust order inflows

• Sequential improvement in Digital Industries EBIT margin is positive

• Continued EBITDA margin compression remains the key negative

reports.text:
NUVAMA ON VENUS PIPES & TUBES

• Rating: Buy | Target: ₹2,100 vs ₹2,000 earlier

• Q1FY27 Revenue/EBITDA/PAT: ↑16%/15%/7% YoY; EBITDA margin at 16.1%

• Domestic sales grew 31% YoY; exports declined 9% due to West Asia crisis

• ₹600 Cr order book + ₹185 Cr LoI for data-centre order

• Management targets 20%+ revenue growth in FY27 and revenue doubling by FY30

• EBITDA margin targeted at 18%+ by FY28

• Nuvama raises TP to ₹2,100 and maintains BUY

reports.text:
JEFFERIES ON HOSPITALS 🏥

• Parliamentary committee report creates another buying opportunity

• Proposals will undergo consultations and may face pushback from hospitals

• Jefferies sees limited earnings risk for hospital operators

• Any sector-led correction should be viewed as a buying opportunity

JEFFERIES ON FINOLEX CABLES

• Rating: Accumulate | Target: ₹1,410 vs ₹1,200 earlier

• Q1 delivered a strong beat

• Electricals growth driven by multiple price hikes over the last 12 months

• Communication segment margins improved on higher optical fibre cable prices and volumes

• Backward integration expected to support margins from Q3 FY27

• FMEG business continues to report positive EBIT

HSBC ON SIEMENS

• Rating: Hold | Target: ₹3,540

• Strong order inflows and execution

• Margin improvement remains elusive

• Higher input costs continue to pressure profitability

• INR depreciation also weighs on margins

INVESTEC ON ZYDUS LIFE 💊

• Rating: Sell | Target: ₹1,090 vs ₹1,000 earlier

• Zydus remains in an investment phase; payoff expected later

• US business investments continue to support the next growth phase

• Acquisitions need upfront investment before synergies materialise

• Innovation remains a key long-term growth driver

• India business growth momentum remains strong

• Target raised to ₹1,090, but rating remains Sell
